q: On a revolving credit facility, interest is charged only on what amount?
explain: A revolver works like a corporate credit card: interest accrues only on what is drawn, while the unused portion typically carries a small commitment fee.
hook: No draw, no interest.

sources.title: Senior Debt | Definition + Loan Characteristics
sources.quote: The interest on a revolver is only charged on the drawn amount, and there is typically only a minor annual commitment fee for the unused portion of the facility

q: What fee compensates a revolver lender for keeping the unused portion of the facility available?
explain: The commitment fee compensates the lender for keeping open access to funds, since interest is only paid when the revolver is drawn.
hook: You pay to keep the door open.

sources.title: Senior Debt | Definition + Loan Characteristics
sources.quote: there is typically only a minor annual commitment fee for the unused portion of the facility

sources.title: Revolving Credit Facility - Definition, How it Works
sources.quote: It compensates the lender for keeping open access to a potential loan, where interest payments are only activated when the revolver is drawn on.

q: Which term loan tranche typically features straight-line amortization and is most often provided by commercial banks?
explain: TLAs amortize in equal repayments down to zero at maturity and are mostly held by banks, often alongside the revolver.
hook: A = Amortizing, held by bAnks.

sources.title: Senior Debt | Definition + Loan Characteristics
sources.quote: TLAs are characterized by straight-line amortization, i.e. equal repayments across the borrowing term until the principal reaches a balance of zero at maturity ... The most frequent lender of TLAs are commercial bank lenders

sources.title: FR03/2024 Leveraged Loans and CLOs Good Practices for Consideration
sources.quote: In some cases a short-term amortising loan often referred to as "Term Loan A" (TLA) is also part of the debt package ... Typically, bank lenders keep the RCF and TLA loans on their balance sheet

q: Term Loan Bs traditionally carry nominal amortization of about what percent of principal per year?
explain: TLBs were traditionally bullet loans or carried nominal amortization, with 1 percent per annum being common; the rest is repaid at maturity.
hook: B = Bullet, with a 1% nibble.

sources.title: Comptroller's Handbook: Leveraged Lending
sources.quote: Traditionally, institutional loans were referred to as term loan B's (TLBs) because they were bullet payment or with nominal (1 percent per annum was common) amortization.

sources.title: Senior Debt | Definition + Loan Characteristics
sources.quote: TLBs are structured with minimal amortization requirements (i.e. 1% to 5% per year) followed by a bullet repayment on the date of maturity

q: Term Loan B tranches are structured specifically for which type of investor?
explain: TLBs are the institutional tranche of a syndicated loan, sold to investors such as CLOs, insurance companies and pension funds.
hook: B is for Buy-side.

sources.title: Comptroller's Handbook: Leveraged Lending
sources.quote: Those tranches (see also) in a syndicated credit that are specifically structured for institutional investors (primarily collateralized loan obligations (CLOs) insurance companies, and pension funds), although there are some banks that may buy institutional credits. Traditionally, institutional loans were referred to as term loan B's (TLBs)

sources.title: FR03/2024 Leveraged Loans and CLOs Good Practices for Consideration
sources.quote: Typically, bank lenders keep the RCF and TLA loans on their balance sheet and distribute part or all of the TLB to institutional investors including CLOs, insurance companies and other banks.

q: What is the lowest Moody's rating that still counts as investment grade?
explain: Corporate bonds rated below Baa3 by Moody's (or below BBB- by S&P and Fitch) are classified as high-yield, or junk, bonds.
hook: Three B-ish letters, then the cliff.

sources.title: High-Yield Bond - Overview, Credit Rating, Real-World Examples
sources.quote: It is a corporate bond with a credit rating below Baa3 from Moody's or BBB- from Standard and Poor's (S&P) and Fitch.

sources.title: High Yield Bonds (Junk Bonds) | Definition + Characteristics
sources.quote: Moody's → Lower than Baa3

q: High-yield bonds are generally structured with what type of interest rate?
explain: High-yield bonds generally pay a higher fixed rate to compensate for default risk, unlike senior bank debt, which is usually floating-rate.
hook: Bonds fix, loans float.

sources.title: High Yield Bonds (Junk Bonds) | Definition + Characteristics
sources.quote: Generally, high yield bonds are unsecured debt instruments with greater upside in potential returns, fixed interest rates, and limited covenants.

sources.title: Subordinated Debt | Financing Definition + Characteristics
sources.quote: Subordinated debt securities such as high-yield bonds (HYBs) are usually priced at a fixed interest rate.

q: Maintenance covenants are a distinguishing feature of which type of debt?
explain: Maintenance covenants were traditionally tied to bank and senior credit facilities, while bonds such as high-yield bonds typically carry incurrence covenants.
hook: Banks maintain; bonds incur.

sources.title: Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia Working Paper 19-41
sources.quote: Maintenance covenants distinguish bank loans from other types of debt, which typically have incurrence covenants.

sources.title: Covenant-Lite Loans (Cov-Lite) | Debt Structure + Characteristics
sources.quote: Ordinarily, maintenance covenants were affiliated with senior credit facilities, whereas incurrence covenants were more associated with high-yield bonds (HYBs).

q: How often is compliance with maintenance covenants typically tested?
explain: Maintenance covenants must be met throughout the loan term and are typically tested at the end of each quarter.
hook: Four check-ups a year.

sources.title: Covenant-Lite Loans (Cov-Lite) | Debt Structure + Characteristics
sources.quote: Further, pressuring the borrower to perform, compliance with maintenance covenants are typically tested for on a quarterly basis.

sources.title: Leverage Ratio Formula and Calculations | Wall Street Prep
sources.quote: Maintenance covenants are contractual agreements requiring the borrower to maintain compliance with certain credit metrics, with periodic testing performed at the end of each quarter.

q: A covenant-lite loan lacks which type of covenant?
explain: Cov-lite loans have bond-like incurrence covenants, if any, rather than traditional maintenance covenants, though they are still secured.
hook: Lite on maintenance.

sources.title: Comptroller's Handbook: Leveraged Lending
sources.quote: Covenant lite — Refers to syndicated loans that have bond-like incurrence covenants (see also), if any covenants, rather than traditional maintenance covenants (see also).

sources.title: Covenant-Lite Loans (Cov-Lite) | Debt Structure + Characteristics
sources.quote: Covenant-lite loans are still secured (i.e. 1 st lien ) but contain incurrence covenants, a feature traditionally more common with bond issuances.

q: If a borrower takes on no new debt but falling EBITDA pushes debt-to-EBITDA above the 5.0x limit, which covenant type is breached?
explain: A maintenance covenant is breached by underperformance alone, while an incurrence covenant is only tested when the borrower takes an action such as raising new debt.
hook: Maintenance trips on its own; incurrence needs an action.

sources.title: Covenant-Lite Loans (Cov-Lite) | Debt Structure + Characteristics
sources.quote: For example, a maintenance covenant could require the borrower to maintain a 5.0x or lower debt-to-EBITDA ratio. If the borrower's debt-to-EBITDA ratio were to exceed 5.0x from underperformance, the borrower is not in compliance with the lending agreement and would be in technical default.

sources.title: Debt Covenants | Lending Types + Loan Examples
sources.quote: However, if the borrower does not participate in any external financing but its debt-to-EBITDA ratio exceeds 5.0x due to a lower EBITDA, the borrower has NOT breached the incurrence covenant (although there may be other covenants in breach).

q: Unitranche debt combines senior debt and what other type of debt into a single facility?
explain: Unitranche blends senior and subordinated debt into one instrument under a single credit agreement, popular in middle-market LBOs.
hook: Uni = one tranche for two layers.

sources.title: Unitranche Debt - Hybrid Loan with Senior and Subordinated Debt
sources.quote: A Unitranche Debt is a hybrid loan structure that combines senior and subordinated debt into one debt instrument.

sources.title: Unitranche Debt | Hybrid Loan Structure + Example
sources.quote: Governed by a single credit agreement , unitranche loans combine senior debt and subordinated debt into one credit facility.

q: What is the term for the single interest rate a unitranche borrower pays, which falls between the senior and subordinated debt rates?
explain: The unitranche rate is a blended rate reflecting the spread of risk between senior and subordinated debt.
hook: Blend the layers, blend the rate.

sources.title: Unitranche Debt - Hybrid Loan with Senior and Subordinated Debt
sources.quote: The borrower of this type of loan pays a blended interest rate that falls between the rate of the senior debt and subordinated debt.

sources.title: Unitranche Debt | Hybrid Loan Structure + Example
sources.quote: The interest rate represents a "blended" rate that should reflect the spread of risk between senior and subordinated debt.

q: In a bifurcated unitranche, which tranche gets priority of payment if certain triggering events occur?
explain: A bifurcated unitranche slices the loan into a first-out and a last-out tranche, with the first-out portion paid first after triggering events.
hook: First out, first paid.

sources.title: Unitranche Debt | Hybrid Loan Structure + Example
sources.quote: As for the latter, a bifurcated unitranche slices the loan into two distinct tranches: 1. "First-Out" Tranche 2. "Last-Out" Tranche The first-out portion gets priority of payment if certain triggering events occur.

q: Which document governs priority, voting rights and economics among first-out and last-out lenders in a unitranche?
explain: The Agreement Among Lenders sets the payment waterfall and allocation of fees and interest between unitranche lenders, functioning like an intercreditor agreement.
hook: AAL keeps all lenders aligned.

sources.title: Unitranche Debt | Hybrid Loan Structure + Example
sources.quote: The AAL functions like an inter-creditor agreement by governing the priority ranking, voting rights, and different economics among creditors.

q: With paid-in-kind (PIK) interest, the accrued interest is added to what?
explain: PIK interest is not paid in cash; it accrues to the ending debt balance, so the principal grows and compounds over time.
hook: Pay in kind = pay with more debt.

sources.title: PIK Interest (Paid-in-Kind) | Formula + Calculator
sources.quote: PIK interest stands for "Paid-in-Kind" and is defined as the amount of interest expense charged by a lender which accrues towards the ending debt balance (principal).

q: What is a note called that gives the borrower the option to pay interest in cash or in kind?
explain: A toggle note lets the borrower switch between cash-pay interest and PIK; toggling to PIK usually raises the rate to compensate holders.
hook: Flip the switch: cash or kind.

sources.title: Comptroller's Handbook: Leveraged Lending
sources.quote: Toggle note — A toggle note gives the borrower the option of cash pay interest or payment in kind (see also).

sources.title: PIK Interest (Paid-in-Kind) | Formula + Calculator
sources.quote: If a PIK toggle is in place, the decision on whether interest expense is paid-in-cash or PIK becomes more of a discretionary decision made on the specific circumstances regarding the credit health of the borrower.

q: Notes with a $1 million beginning balance accrue 8% PIK interest; what is the ending balance after one year?
explain: PIK interest equals the PIK rate times the beginning balance ($1m x 8% = $80k), which accrues to principal, giving $1.08m.
hook: Interest joins the principal.

sources.title: PIK Interest (Paid-in-Kind) | Formula + Calculator
sources.quote: Therefore, we can see how the $80k of interest accrued towards the principal for the ending balance calculation for Year 1 for a total of $1.08m.

q: Using FCCR = (EBITDA - Capex - Cash Taxes) / (Cash Interest + Mandatory Amortization), what is the FCCR with EBITDA $20m, capex $2.5m, cash taxes $5m, interest $2.25m and mandatory repayment $4m?
explain: Covenant-adjusted EBITDA is $12.5m and fixed charges are $6.25m, so FCCR = 2.0x.

sources.title: Fixed Charge Coverage Ratio (FCCR) | Formula + Calculator
sources.quote: Fixed Charge Coverage Ratio = (EBITDA – Capex – Cash Taxes) ÷ (Cash Interest Expense + Mandatory Debt Amortization) ... Fixed Charge Coverage Ratio = $12.5 million ÷ $6.25 million = 2.0x

q: A company has EBIT of $100 million and interest expense of $20 million; what is its EBIT interest coverage ratio?
explain: Interest coverage ratio = EBIT / net interest expense = $100m / $20m = 5.0x; higher ratios signal lower default risk.
hook: How many times can EBIT pay the interest?

sources.title: Interest Coverage Ratio (ICR) | Formula + Calculator
sources.quote: For instance, if the EBIT of a company is $100 million while the amount of annual interest expense due is $20 million, the interest coverage ratio is 5.0x.

q: Which credit ratio is calculated by dividing total debt by EBITDA?
explain: The leverage ratio, or debt-to-EBITDA, divides total debt by EBITDA and is a common maintenance covenant metric.
hook: Debt over EBITDA = turns of leverage.

sources.title: Leverage Ratio Formula and Calculations | Wall Street Prep
sources.quote: The leverage ratio—or debt-to-EBITDA ratio—is calculated by dividing the total debt balance by EBITDA in the corresponding period.

q: What is the term for a secured lender's claim on the assets a borrower pledges as collateral?
explain: Senior debt is typically secured, giving the lender a lien on pledged assets that can be seized in default.
hook: Lien = lender leans on the assets.

sources.title: Senior Debt | Definition + Loan Characteristics
sources.quote: Notably, senior debt is secured, meaning that the debt issuance is backed by collateral , i.e. the lender now has a lien (i.e. claim) on the assets pledged by the borrower.

q: Which lenders are more likely to charge fees or prohibit early repayment: senior or subordinated lenders?
explain: Senior lenders rarely penalize prepayment, while subordinated lenders charge prepayment fees or bar early repayment to protect their yield.
hook: Higher yield, harder to repay early.

sources.title: Subordinated Debt | Financing Definition + Characteristics
sources.quote: That said, subordinated debt lenders are more likely to charge fees for borrowers that repay debt ahead of schedule, in an effort to mitigate the loss in return for the lower interest expense (or the lender might prohibit early repayment for a set number of years or the entire borrowing term).

sources.title: Senior Debt | Definition + Loan Characteristics
sources.quote: Further, senior debt can usually be paid back early with no (or minimal) prepayment fees, while subordinated lenders charge higher penalties in the case of prepayment.

q: What type of call protection bars the issuer from redeeming a bond during a set period, such as the first ten years?
explain: Hard call protection limits the time frame during which a bond may be redeemed early, assuring investors the coupon for that period.
hook: Hard = hard no.

sources.title: Call Protection - Overview, How Callable Bonds Work, Types
sources.quote: For example, a 20-year bond may include a hard call protection that only allows the issuer to redeem the bonds after the first ten years of the bond's life.

q: What type of call protection requires the issuer to pay a premium over face value to redeem a bond early?
explain: Soft call protection requires a premium over face value for early redemption and is often stair-stepped, with higher premiums for earlier calls.
hook: Soft = you can, but it costs you.

sources.title: Call Protection - Overview, How Callable Bonds Work, Types
sources.quote: The second form is referred to as soft call protection. ... The provision requires the bond issuer to pay bond buyers a premium over and above the bond's face value if it elects to redeem the bond before maturity.

q: Under a make-whole call provision, the redemption payment is based on the present value of what?
explain: A make-whole call pays the greater of par and the net present value of the remaining coupon payments and principal, and can be exercised at any time.
hook: Make the lender whole for what they would have earned.

sources.title: Make-Whole Call Provision - Overview, How it Works
sources.quote: The amount that the issuer must pay the lender is determined by calculating the net present value of the coupon payments and the principal that the lender would've received if the bond was not retired early.
